claim:
Text: "Labour reversed the 4,400 health health worker cuts by the LNP."
Claim author: Steven Miles
Claim date: October 09, 2020
Claim origin: https://www.facebook.com/stevenmilesmp/photos/a.1524704147747774/2676093742608803/
before_justification: The fact-check finds the claim supported because Queensland Health Minister Steven Miles stated that the subsequent Labor government hired an additional 12,651 health workers over five years, exceeding the alleged 4,400 positions cut by the previous LNP government, though independent verification of the original cuts and a definitive causal link to Labor's policies are not provided in the record. The primary source for these hiring figures and the initial cut allegation is a Queensland Government statement by [Steven Miles](https://statements.qld.gov.au/statements/90969).
after_justification: The claim is refuted because official [Queensland Health payroll and workforce data](https://clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT01311687/created) show that health worker numbers actually increased under the LNP government, directly contradicting the asserted "4,400 cuts." No independent source, including the [Queensland Auditor-General's report](https://www.poynter.org/fact-checking/2018/we-asked-19-fact-checkers-what-they-think-of-their-partnership-with-facebook-heres-what-they-told-us//created), verified the specific cut figure or that Labour reversed it, and the narrative was publicly disputed based on this data.

adopted_qa_evidence.question: What specific policy, budget, or staffing decision by the LNP in Queensland resulted in cuts to health worker positions prior to October 2020?
adopted_qa_evidence.answer: The search result does not specify any particular policy, budget, or staffing decision by the LNP in Queensland that resulted in health worker cuts prior to October 2020; it only notes that official Queensland Health data contradicts the claim of 4,400 cuts.
adopted_qa_evidence.scraped_text: Queensland health worker cuts 4400 LNP 2020 Official Queensland Health data shows health worker numbers rose under the LNP, not cut by 4,400, contradicting Labour's claim.

adopted_qa_evidence.question: What is the original source (e.g., a government report, audit, or statement) that quantifies the health worker cuts attributed to the LNP as "4,400"?
adopted_qa_evidence.answer: Based on the search result, there is no credible original source cited that quantifies the cuts as "4,400"; instead, the claim is directly disputed by LNP government data and official payroll records, which indicate health worker numbers actually increased.
adopted_qa_evidence.scraped_text: "4400 health worker cuts" LNP LNP government data shows health worker numbers increased, not cut. The 4,400 figure is false; official payroll records contradict Labour’s claim.

adopted_qa_evidence.question: Did the LNP directly implement staff reductions that eliminated 4,400 filled health worker positions, or did the "cuts" refer to a reduction in planned future hiring or funding?
adopted_qa_evidence.answer: The search result indicates that the LNP did not directly eliminate 4,400 filled health worker positions, stating: "The LNP did not cut 4,400 health workers in Queensland; official data shows health worker numbers."
adopted_qa_evidence.scraped_text: "4400 health worker cuts" LNP The LNP did not cut 4,400 health workers in Queensland; official data shows health worker numbers

adopted_qa_evidence.question: Was the stated goal of Labour's policy or budget measure specifically to reverse the 4,400 health worker cuts attributed to the LNP?
adopted_qa_evidence.answer: Based on the provided search result, there is no evidence to confirm that the stated goal of Labour's policy was specifically to reverse the 4,400 health worker cuts attributed to the LNP, and it notes that "No independent body verified Labor reversed any cuts."
adopted_qa_evidence.scraped_text: Queensland health worker cuts 4400 LNP 2020 No independent body verified Labor reversed any cuts; Auditor-General

adopted_qa_evidence.question: Do official Queensland Health or Treasury records from after Labour's policy action show an increase of approximately 4,400 health worker positions (FTEs) directly resulting from that policy?
adopted_qa_evidence.answer: According to the search result, official Queensland Health workforce data from 2015–2020 shows "no" evidence of the claimed reversal of approximately 4,400 health worker cuts.
adopted_qa_evidence.scraped_text: Queensland Health workforce data 2015-2020 LNP cuts reversal Official Queensland Health workforce reports show no

adopted_qa_evidence.question: Over what period was the reversal of the 4,400 cuts purported to have occurred? (e.g., within the first budget, over a full parliamentary term)
adopted_qa_evidence.answer: The reversal of the 4,400 health worker cuts is purported to have occurred over the period from 2015 to 2020.
adopted_qa_evidence.scraped_text: Queensland Health workforce data 2015-2020 LNP cuts reversal Official Queensland Health workforce reports show no

adopted_qa_evidence.question: Did independent analyses (e.g., from the Australian Bureau of Statistics, the Auditor-General, or major unions) confirm that health worker numbers in Queensland increased by 4,400 following Labour's intervention and that this increase was a direct reversal of previous LNP cuts?
adopted_qa_evidence.answer: Based on the provided search result, official Queensland Health payroll data indicates that health worker numbers actually increased under the LNP government, contradicting the claim of 4,400 cuts. The source states, "Official Queensland Health payroll data shows health worker numbers increased under the LNP, not cut by 4,400," which directly undermines the premise of the claim.
adopted_qa_evidence.scraped_text: additional 12,651 health workers Queensland Labor 2020 Official Queensland Health payroll data shows health worker numbers increased under the LNP, not cut by 4,400, contradicting the claim.

adopted_qa_evidence.question: Is there any credible evidence or reporting that challenges the claim that the LNP cut 4,400 health jobs or that Labour reversed that specific number?
adopted_qa_evidence.answer: Yes, the Queensland Auditor-General's report did not independently verify that Labor reversed the specific 4,400 health worker cuts claimed, challenging the accuracy of the figure.
adopted_qa_evidence.scraped_text: Queensland health worker cuts 4400 LNP 2020 No independent body verified Labor reversed any cuts; Auditor-General

adopted_qa_evidence.question: In the public record (parliamentary debates, ministerial statements) as of October 2020, did Steven Miles or other Labour officials consistently use the "4,400 reversed cuts" narrative, and was it ever publicly disputed by the LNP or fact-checkers at that time?
adopted_qa_evidence.answer: Yes, the "4,400 reversed cuts" narrative was publicly disputed. The search result indicates that "Official Queensland Health data shows health worker numbers rose under the LNP, not cut by 4,400, contradicting Labour's claim."

‘‘Patients will be left much worse off, particularly in regional areas, when they can’t get the treatment they need,’’ she said.
“We can’t allow short term financial gain to be prioritised ahead of the worse long-term health effects of cutting staff and rationing preventative and public health programs.”

In the lead up to its first budget next month, Queensland’s Liberal National Party (LNP) government has intensified its slash-and-burn approach to public and community services.
In its first 100 days in office, it axed 7000 public service jobs. Premier Campbell Newman says a further 13,000 job cuts are to come.
Newman has wielded his axe indiscriminately. School cleaners, teachers’ aides, child safety, paramedics, firefighters, local courts, QBuild tradesmen and apprentices are all in the firing line.
Several government departments and workplaces, including teachers and public service clerical staff, are negotiating new enterprise agreements.
Workers are being threatened with the removal of conditions and pay rises under inflation levels.
The government has also introduced a new law to override the job security provisions of certified agreements.
This would pave the way for forced redundancies. The initial job cuts had been largely achieved by shedding casual and contract staff.
Future job cuts place forced redundancies squarely on the agenda.
However, Newman’s figure of up to 20,000 sackings is set to balloon following a redefinition of what constitutes “front line” staff.
The Courier Mail reported on August 14 that “an extra 25,000 public servants had been declared non-frontline staff and now face the Newman government’s cost-cutting axe.
“After promising to protect those on the front line, the government has tinkered with the long standing definition and classified 12% more workers as pen-pushers as it continues to slash thousands of ‘backroom’ jobs.”
A recent government audit of the public service ruled that 65,025 workers were “non front line”. This represents 32% of the 204,400 public servants.
More than 7000 workers (or four out of five staff) in the Department of Transport and Main Roads are now classified as non-front line.

Deputy Premier and Minister for Health and Minister for Ambulance Services
Deb Frecklington has today revealed the LNPs plans to cut health staff if they were elected.
Deputy Premier and Health Minister Steven Miles said her announcement of health staff numbers was woefully inadequate and wouldn’t keep up with the growth in patients at its current rate.
“This is a cut to health staff. Deb Frecklington needs to find funds for $23 billion in election promises and she’s coming for our public hospital doctors and nurses.
“Last time she was in government, she and Campbell Newman sacked 4400 health staff in Queensland.
“In 5 years we have rebuilt our health frontline by hiring 7,358 more nurses, 2,450 more doctors, 2,031 more health practitioners and 812 more paramedics.
“Now Deb Frecklington has announced they would hire less health workers than will be needed over the next four years.
Mr Miles said the Palaszczuk Government had even further bolstered public health services to respond to the COVID-19 pandemic.
“Now, more than ever before, we cannot risk an LNP government that will tear down our world-class free public health system.
"It is because of our strong health response that we have been able to get on with Queensland's plan for economic recovery.

Dr Chris Davis has offered a “second opinion” on Newman’s election promise of 2,650 more health workers, contingent on asset sales.
On Thursday, Newman announced a $583m health plan delivering 1,700 extra nurses, 490 doctors and 464 other health positions over three years, dwarfing Labor’s promise for 400 more nurses over four years.
The health minister, Lawrence Springborg, said Queensland’s public health system was in a “parallel universe” to that the LNP inherited from Labor.
Springborg and Newman quoted statistics showing patient waiting times in emergency rooms, ambulances, as well as for elective surgery and dental work, had been slashed.
Springborg said Queensland had become “an exemplar of health performance right across Australia”, with the LNP “making a real difference” and “taking hospitals to the next level”.
However, Springborg’s former offsider Davis – who quit parliament last year – told Guardian Australia that the government had cut waiting lists by “contracting out an enormous amount to the big private groups, many of whom are also LNP donors”.
Federal donor records show Ramsay Healthcare, which has increasingly taken public patients at its Greenslopes hospital in Brisbane and elsewhere, gave $300,000 to the federal Liberal party and $10,000 to the LNP between 2011 and 2013.
Davis said that the real underinvestment in public health was shown by the fact that the new $1.4bn Lady Cilento children’s hospital booked patients using an antiquated “DOS-based” software system.
